title: Three Ways to Scale Intelligence
description: Three paths to stronger LLMs: greater investment, better efficiency, and new scaling dimensions.

stages.label: Overview
stages.title: Three ways to scale intelligence.
stages.body: Scaling is central to progress in LLMs. We explore three paths: invest more along existing dimensions, improve computational efficiency, and find new dimensions for growth.

stages.label: Route 01
stages.title: Invest more. Raise the ceiling.
stages.body: Increasing model parameters, training data, and reasoning effort can extend capabilities along an existing scaling path. As returns diminish, each further gain requires greater investment.

stages.label: Route 02
stages.title: The same capability, at lower cost.
stages.body: Improving efficiency means reaching comparable capabilities with fewer resources. Quantization, sparse attention, speculative decoding, and adaptive compute offer different ways to reduce memory use, computation, or latency.

stages.label: Route 03
stages.title: Find a new scaling dimension.
stages.body: Model size and data scale have long driven LLM progress. Models such as o1 highlighted another dimension: test-time compute. We explore further possibilities, including loop depth, adaptive computation, and context information density.

chartDescriptions: Black shows the current relationship between cost and intelligence. Purple extends it, green improves efficiency, and blue introduces a new scaling dimension.
The purple curve extends the current path: further gains in intelligence require increasingly higher costs.
The green curve offers greater intelligence at intermediate costs and meets the black curve at the same endpoint.
Blue branches extend different points on the black curve along a new scaling dimension. Their outer envelope shows the best result at each budget.
axes: Cost on the horizontal axis; intelligence on the vertical axis.
projectsLead: We pursue these paths through joint optimization across algorithms and systems.
